_doc: Maximum-quality enterprise analytic blueprint for India Energy Statistics. 3 topics, 5 chapters, 7 sections, 7 questions, ~25 components. Full entity hierarchy with inheritance tracing, complete per-question metadata, BI-agent-ready analytical questions, formula catalog, and officer controls.

templateMeta.name: India Energy Resources — Enterprise Report v2
templateMeta.description: Enterprise-grade energy template covering conventional reserves (coal, lignite, hydrocarbons) and renewable potential (wind, solar, hydro, biomass) with state-level rankings, regional aggregation, composition analysis, and cross-cutting ratio metrics. Full hierarchy entity tracing and BI-agent-ready question contracts.

statisticalContext.ministry: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
dataSources: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

glossary.CMPDI: Central Mine Planning and Design Institute
glossary.MNRE: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
glossary.Proved Reserves: Reserves established with the highest degree of geological confidence.
glossary.Indicated Reserves: Reserves estimated with reasonable geological confidence.
glossary.Inferred Reserves: Reserves estimated with low geological confidence.
glossary.Reserve Category: Geological confidence classification: Proved, Indicated, or Inferred.

topics.title: Conventional Energy Reserves
topics.officerSummary: Covers coal, lignite, and hydrocarbon (crude oil, natural gas) reserves by state, region, and geological confidence category.

chapters.title: Coal & Lignite Reserves
chapters.officerSummary: State-wise coal and lignite reserves with breakdown by geological confidence (Proved/Indicated/Inferred). Covers 12 coal-bearing states.

questions.intent: Establish the geographic concentration of coal reserves and identify dominant coal-bearing states.
questions.questionText: Rank States/UTs by total coal reserves showing regional concentration and identify the top 5 contributors.
questions.officerIntent: Show which states dominate India's coal reserves, grouped by region so the East's dominance is immediately visible.

caveatsWhenDegraded: Note: States with null Coal values excluded from ranking.

provenanceRequirements.sourceAttribution: Geological Survey of India / CMPDI estimates

reviewChecklist: Verify Jharkhand and Odisha appear in top 3
Confirm East region dominates
Check null handling for non-coal states
Validate total = sum of category columns

narrativeTemplate.exampleOutput: India's coal reserves are concentrated in the eastern states, with Odisha (84,500 MT) and Jharkhand (83,152 MT) together accounting for nearly half of the national total.

chartSpec.title: Top Coal-bearing States by Total Reserves

questions.intent: Analyze the geological confidence distribution of reserves to assess exploration maturity.
questions.questionText: How are India's coal and lignite reserves distributed across Proved, Indicated, and Inferred categories, and what does this imply for extraction readiness?
questions.officerIntent: Show that most of India's reserves are in the Proved category (exploration-mature), giving confidence for extraction planning.

caveatsWhenDegraded: Note: States without reserve classification excluded.

reviewChecklist: Verify Proved + Indicated + Inferred = Total for each state
Confirm Proved share > 50% nationally
Check that category nulls align with non-coal states

narrativeTemplate.exampleOutput: Proved reserves constitute 63% of India's total coal reserves (2,21,700 MT of 3,52,900 MT), indicating a high level of exploration maturity across major coal-bearing states.

chapters.title: Hydrocarbon Reserves
chapters.officerSummary: Crude oil and natural gas reserves distribution. Concentrated in very few states (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Assam).

questions.intent: Identify the few states with hydrocarbon reserves and quantify their holdings.
questions.questionText: Which states hold crude oil and natural gas reserves, and how concentrated are these resources geographically?

filters.condition: ent_crude_oil IS NOT NULL OR ent_natural_gas IS NOT NULL

questions.officerIntent: Highlight that hydrocarbons are extremely concentrated — only 4 states have reserves. This contrasts with coal's wider distribution.

provenanceRequirements.sourceAttribution: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas

reviewChecklist: Verify only 4 states have data
Confirm Assam and Gujarat dominate
Note different units: MT vs BCM

tableSpec.title: Hydrocarbon Reserves by State
tableSpec.footnote: Source: MoPNG. Units: Crude Oil (MT), Natural Gas (BCM)

content.sourceName: Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas / Directorate General of Hydrocarbons
content.coverage: Data for producing states only (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Assam, Andhra Pradesh)

topics.title: Renewable Energy Potential
topics.officerSummary: State-wise assessed potential for wind, solar, small hydro, biomass, cogeneration, and large hydro. Source mix composition analysis.

chapters.title: Source-wise Renewable Capacity
chapters.officerSummary: Detailed state-wise potential for each renewable source. Wind and solar dominate but hydro and biomass fill niche roles.

questions.intent: Compare the two dominant renewable sources across states to reveal geographic specialization.
questions.questionText: Compare wind and solar assessed potential across India's states, identifying which states specialize in each source and the overall regional pattern.
questions.officerIntent: Show that wind is concentrated in western/southern coastal states while solar is distributed more broadly, with Rajasthan leading solar massively.
reviewChecklist: Verify Karnataka leads wind
Confirm Rajasthan leads solar
Check Maharashtra in both top lists

chartSpec.title: Wind vs Solar Potential by State (Top 10)

tableSpec.title: State-wise Wind, Solar & Total Renewable Potential (MW)

questions.intent: Document niche renewable sources that play significant roles in specific states (Himalayan hydro, agricultural biomass).
questions.questionText: What is the state-wise assessed potential for small hydro, biomass, cogeneration-bagasse, and large hydro, and which states specialize in these niche sources?
questions.officerIntent: Show that large hydro is dominated by NE/Himalayan states, biomass by sugarcane states (UP, Maharashtra), small hydro by hill states.
reviewChecklist: Verify Arunachal Pradesh leads large hydro
Confirm Himachal Pradesh leads small hydro
Check UP for cogeneration-bagasse

content.description: Several states show zero potential for specific sources (e.g., Wind=0 for landlocked NE states). These are valid zeros (no assessed potential) rather than missing data.

chapters.title: Renewable Source Mix & Dominance
chapters.officerSummary: National composition of renewable potential by source type. SHARE formula analysis showing solar and wind dominance.

questions.intent: Quantify the national renewable energy mix to show which sources have the greatest potential.
questions.questionText: What share does each renewable source (wind, solar, small hydro, biomass, cogeneration, large hydro) contribute to India's total assessed renewable potential?
questions.officerIntent: Demonstrate that solar + wind together account for >80% of total renewable potential, making them the primary pillars of India's energy transition.
reviewChecklist: Verify sum of parts ≈ Total Renewable for each state
Confirm solar share > 40%
Confirm wind share > 25%
Check that Large Hydro is significant (>10%)

formulaSpec.displayAs: Solar share of total renewable potential
Wind share of total renewable potential

topics.title: Cross-Cutting Regional Analysis
topics.officerSummary: Regional energy endowment comparison (conventional vs renewable), data sources, methodology notes, and coverage limitations.

chapters.title: Regional Energy Endowment
chapters.officerSummary: Compares conventional and renewable resources by region, showing energy specialization patterns.

questions.intent: Reveal regional specialization patterns — East for coal, South/West for renewables, North for hydro.
questions.questionText: How do conventional and renewable energy resources distribute across India's regions, and what is the ratio of renewable to conventional potential per region?
questions.officerIntent: Highlight that East = coal powerhouse, South/West = renewable leaders, North/NE = hydro-dependent. The ratio metric is an index, not a physical conversion.
reviewChecklist: Verify East region coal total > 200,000 MT
Confirm South leads renewable total
Note that RATIO is cross-unit index not physical conversion

chapters.title: Data Provenance & Methodology
chapters.officerSummary: Data sources, measurement units, coverage limitations, and methodological notes for reproducibility and audit.

questions.intent: Provide full transparency on data provenance for audit compliance and reproducibility.
questions.questionText: What are the data sources, measurement units, coverage scope, and known limitations of this energy statistics compilation?
questions.officerIntent: Satisfy MoSPI audit requirements by documenting every source, unit, and known gap.
reviewChecklist: All 4 source agencies mentioned
All 3 unit types defined (MT, MW, BCM)
Null percentages documented
Geographic coverage noted (18 states)

content.title: Methodology & Aggregation Rules
content.description: Coal/lignite reserves are reported as geological estimates (MT) classified by confidence level. Renewable potential is assessed capacity (MW) based on resource surveys. Regional aggregations are simple sums. SHARE formulas divide at the same grain (state or national) then display as percentage.
assumptions: Renewable potential = technically feasible capacity, not installed
limitations: Single time period — no trend analysis possible
State boundaries as of 2025 Census delimitation
Hydrocarbons data available for producing states only

sources.agency: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas (MoPNG)
sources.covers: Crude oil and natural gas reserves

content.coverage: 18 major states/UTs with significant energy resources. Period: 2025.

terms.definition: Million Tonnes — unit for coal, lignite, and crude oil reserves
Megawatt — unit for renewable energy potential (assessed capacity)
Billion Cubic Metres — unit for natural gas reserves
Reserves established with the highest degree of geological confidence under UNFC-2009
Technically feasible energy generation capacity based on resource surveys, not installed capacity

content.description: Significant null values exist in measure columns for states without relevant resources. Coal: 33% null (6 states have no coal deposits). Lignite: 78% null (only 3 states). Crude Oil/Natural Gas: 78% null (only 4 producing states). These are true zeros (no resource) rather than data collection failures.
content.impactScope: States without the relevant resource type show null; excluded from ranking/composition analysis for that resource.
